evidence.title: MM-IssueLoc: A Controlled Benchmark for Evaluating Visual Evidence in Multimodal Repository-Level Issue Localization
evidence.abstract: Real repository issues routinely include visual evidence such as screenshots, error dialogs, rendered UI states, and logs, yet repository-level issue localization is evaluated mostly as a text-only task. Existing multimodal SE benchmarks evaluate end-to-end repair, entangling localization with patch synthesis and obscuring whether visual input helped, hurt, or was ignored. We introduce MM-IssueLoc, a controlled benchmark and evaluation protocol for repository-level localization with visual evidence. MM-IssueLoc contains 652 issue-PR instances across 23 languages, with annotations for 7 image categories and 4 relevance levels. It provides file-level and function-level gold labels, paired text-only and with-image evaluation, and VCE-based diagnostics that convert images into structured textual evidence. We evaluate LLM-based and retrieval-based systems, including MM-IssueLoc-VL-Emb as a controlled multimodal retriever. Results show that existing systems remain far from reliable multimodal repository localization: the strongest agent reaches 38.96 file Acc@5 and 22.45 function Acc@10, while the strongest retriever reaches 33.86 function Acc@10. Cross-benchmark comparisons show that high localization scores on text-dominant SWE benchmarks do not transfer cleanly to multimodal issue localization. title: NavCMPO: Critic-Guided MeanFlow Policy Optimization for Adaptive Navigation
abstract: End-to-end diffusion-based policies have demonstrated strong performance in mapless visual navigation, but their iterative denoising process introduces substantial inference latency, while behavior cloning limits performance to the quality of expert demonstrations. We present NavCMPO, a two-stage adaptive navigation framework that combines few-step MeanFlow trajectory generation, critic-guided refinement, and reinforcement learning fine-tuning. During pre-training, an obstacle proximity prediction task encourages the visual representation to capture obstacle-aware spatial information. To compensate for the degradation in obstacle avoidance caused by few-step generation, Critic-Guided Trajectory Refinement (CGTR) uses gradients from a critic trained with obstacle-point-cloud supervision to refine intermediate trajectories. During adaptation, the MeanFlow policy is fine-tuned using Proximal Policy Optimization with behavior-cloning regularization, while the critic is updated to accommodate embodiment-specific observation changes. Under a matched training budget on the InternVLA-N1 benchmark, NavCMPO achieves an average success rate of 74.7\%, exceeding the retrained NavDP baseline by 6.4 percentage points, while reducing inference latency from 85\,ms to 60\,ms. Experiments on a Unitree Go2 further demonstrate effective sim-to-real transfer.

title: A Targeted Causal-Break Test for Engineered History Dependence on a Superconducting Quantum Processor
abstract: This archive contains the Version 1 public release of the targeted causal-break testing protocol together with the manuscript, supplementary material, registered experimental protocols, QASM circuits, analysis procedures, and documentation associated with the study. The work demonstrates a low-setting experimental methodology for testing engineered history dependence on superconducting quantum hardware while explicitly preserving preregistration records, failed controls, confirmatory replications, calibration experiments, and protocol revisions.

title: METAFOR exploratory landscape analysis features for continuous optimization benchmarks (dimensions 10 and 50)
abstract: This dataset provides exploratory landscape analysis (ELA) features for continuous-optimization benchmark instances evaluated through METAFOR in dimensions 10 and 50. The instance registry contains 456 problem-dimension records. Four records with unbounded search domains were intentionally excluded from sampling, leaving 452 usable records. Each usable record was sampled in 100 independent repetitions, producing 45,200 successful per-repeat feature observations and 452 aggregate records. The dataset contains portable sampling manifests, raw and standardized per-repeat ELA features, per-instance aggregate means and standard deviations, scaler parameters, extraction metadata, checksums, and validation reports. A total of 107 ELA feature columns were extracted using flacco; 99 contain at least one finite value. Raw sampled decision vectors, objective-value files, intermediate feature chunks, and visualization outputs are intentionally excluded from this compact core dataset. Sampling commands, seeds, point counts, statuses, elapsed times, software provenance, and excluded-data details are recorded in the included manifests.

title: Effect of Intermediate Task Scaling on XLM-R Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Performance in XTREME
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: What is the effect of scaling the number of intermediate tasks (e.g., 5 vs. 10) on the zero-shot cross-lingual performance (accuracy) of XLM-R on the XTREME benchmark? Autonomous synthesis report generated by Assignee Research. Tribunal consensus score: 9.0/10.
